key_insight: ScienceIDE turns scientific code repositories into programmable environments that AI agents can learn and act in, rather than treating them as static code archives. The core idea is to make scientific knowledge executable, testable, and agent-friendly.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the "scientific experience bottleneck": scientific code is rich in knowledge but hard for agents to use because of fragmented toolchains, implicit domain conventions, and specialized correctness criteria.
method: Builds infrastructure that converts scientific codebases into agent-learnable environments.
Uses expert-defined scientific guidance to specify tasks, interfaces, and correctness checks.
Standardizes interactions so agents can explore, execute, and learn from real scientific workflows.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this creates a practical bridge between foundation models and real scientific software ecosystems. It could improve agent reliability, domain adaptation, and automation in research-heavy coding tasks.

paper_title: ScienceIDE: Turning World's Scientific Codebase into Agent Learnable Environments
paper_authors: Hejia Geng, Zesen Huang, Haoyang Li, Wenbin Li, Koutian Wu
